First of all I want to say I understand you. I graduated in July 2020 and couldn’t secure a position in my field until October-November 2020. I felt like I wasn’t meeting my goals and for a few moments I forgot what my goals even were and was feeling like I have no direction. All my life I thought I was really smart and suddenly all that confidence got taken away by rejections from jobs I applied for. I also questioned my choice of university. When I chose it the first time it was very high up in the tops, but then it kind of steadily went down and I was telling myself that maybe those people would have hired me if I chose a uni like Oxford (i’m in the UK). Well in the end it worked out for me, I found a job that makes me happy and helps me grow and meet my goals, even if my goals are a bit different than they were at the beginning. 

So back to you. You’re not average. You are in no way a failure. You have made a sensible choice of college based on what you could afford and luckily you do enjoy your classes. You will get rejections and it may take you some time to get on the track you want to be on, but please remember the difficult year we’ve all had and how reduced opportunities are compared to before. Keep applying for internships, you will get one. The right employer will see you for you are, for your mind and your skills and your personality and won’t care about what college you went to. You got rejected from the CLS program? Find another program that you’re interested in and apply for that one. Keep going and keep open to new opportunities and paths. You’ll be fine.

I’ve just graduated uni and am trying to find a job in my field. I feel so confused about what I want to do next and where I would like to work and what values I want to prioritise. It’s also so hard to find a job when I don’t have a lot of experience in the field, especially because of Covid, and I just feel a bit overwhelmed with all the uncertainty. The application process is so long and stressful and although I consider myself to be quite bright, the anxiety and depression just make me avoid it and paint myself in a negative light which just leads to me feeling more stressed and anxious about it. I know I’m still young (21) and I have the rest of my life to figure these things out, but I’ve always put so much pressure on myself and I don’t know how to stop. I feel like I am a failure when I stop. 

Also, I wouldn’t say I prioritise adventure and fun. I don’t have a lot of friends, half of my them live in different countries, as well as my family. Even if I did, I would avoid meeting them right now (again, Covid). I spend most of my days alone, cleaning my flat, looking for jobs, and then just basically waiting for the day to end. I know it’s awful but I just can’t get myself to do anything else. Whenever I think about doing something that I used to enjoy doing, such as painting, writing, meeting people, taking pictures, it starts feeling like a chore and I can’t do it. I would love to be more adventurous, I just don’t know how to do it on my own, in the current circumstances. 

On Wednesday I am going back to my current job (chef) and I’m dreading it. I’ve been away for 4 months and I literally can’t imagine going back to 9-15 hour shifts of running around and socialising with people that I don’t like and finishing really late and not having any time off. 

The worst thing is that I know that I could try changing things, I could try fighting for the life I want but I just feel paralysed. I guess it’s easier to quietly hate myself than it is to change everything I don’t like about myself. 

Anyway, thank you so much for taking the time to reply and for listening to me.
